The test contains multiple specific assertions (checks on the transposed graph's vertex count, original graph's vertex count, and that instances are distinct), which verify multiple relevant properties rather than a single superficial check.
There are no @Ignore/@Disabled annotations, no commented-out @Test methods, and no TODO markers visible; the test is active and runnable.
The class-level Javadoc includes a Traceability section with 'REQ-GRAFO-001', explicitly linking the tests to a requirement ID.

practices_evaluation.practice_title: Rigorous Use of Performance and Security Tests
practices_evaluation.justification: This is a unit functional test; there are no performance or security tests expected here and no timing/security annotations are present, so the practice is not applicable to this method.
The test method name 'test8' is generic and does not describe the scenario or expected outcome. Although comments exist, the naming convention requirement is not met.

practices_evaluation.practice_title: Small Footprint of Test Code Generation
practices_evaluation.justification: The presence of EvoSuite-specific runner annotations and a generic test name 'test8' are strong indicators of auto-generated tests; this suggests generated patterns remain and the test naming is not intention-revealing.

practices_evaluation.practice_title: Complete Prioritization of Test Case Design
practices_evaluation.justification: The test includes Given-When-Then comments and descriptive assertion messages which indicate design intent and care in specifying the scenario, consistent with BDD-style structure.

practices_evaluation.practice_title: Responsible Addition of Test Code Maintenance
practices_evaluation.justification: The test exercises public APIs only (constructor, insereAresta, grafoTransposto, numVertices) and does not reference private fields or use reflection, keeping it focused on observable behavior.
Assertions are specific (assertEquals with descriptive messages and assertNotSame), not generic assertTrue/assertFalse, and include helpful failure messages.
The test includes concise Given-When-Then comments that clarify intent without overwhelming the code. There is no commented-out code or excessive comments.
The test uses deterministic operations only (no Random, System.currentTimeMillis, Thread.sleep, or external dependencies). It relies on in-memory objects and local state.

practices_evaluation.practice_title: Complete Avoidance of Test Side Effects
practices_evaluation.justification: Test manipulates only local Grafo instances and does not write files, modify static state, or perform persistent operations; there is no need for explicit cleanup here.

practices_evaluation.practice_title: Suitable Utilization of Test Labels and Categories
practices_evaluation.justification: The class is annotated with @Category(UnitTest.class), providing meaningful categorization that supports selective execution.

PRINCIPLE: Tests should focus on a single requirement/behavior with one Arrange-Act-Assert. RATIONALE: Single-focus tests make root causes easier to find. EVALUATION CRITERIA: Compliant if exactly one Act operation and one clear AAA block. DECISION RULES: 1) Count distinct Act operations. 2) If >1, non-compliant. 3) If only one method call tested, compliant. ANALYSIS: The method calls grafo0.insereAresta(...) and grafo0.retiraAresta(...). Although insereAresta may be setup, there are two distinct public method calls interacting with the graph in the method body and multiple assertions verifying both the result of retiraAresta and graph state. Given ambiguity and the rule to be conservative, this is treated as testing more than one operation in one method. VERDICT: non-compliant.

PRINCIPLE: Tests should not depend on other tests. RATIONALE: Enables parallel and order-independent execution. EVALUATION CRITERIA: Compliant if using only local variables or @Before/@After for setup/teardown. DECISION RULES: 1) Check for @Before/@After. 2) If tests use only local variables, mark compliant. ANALYSIS: This test uses only local variables and does not modify static or shared state within the shown method. No test-order dependence is visible. VERDICT: compliant

practices_evaluation.practice_title: Coverage of Normal and Exceptional Flows
practices_evaluation.justification: PRINCIPLE: Tests should cover both happy path and error/exception scenarios. RATIONALE: Ensures robustness under invalid inputs or failures. EVALUATION CRITERIA: Compliant if there are at least two tests per method: happy path and error case (or use of assertThrows/@Test(expected)). DECISION RULES: 1) If all tests only use valid inputs and expect success, mark non-compliant. 2) Look for assertThrows or @Test(expected=...). ANALYSIS: Only a single happy-path-style test is present; there are no tests for invalid inputs, nulls, or exception cases. VERDICT: non-compliant.

PRINCIPLE: Tests should validate min/max/just-outside boundary inputs. RATIONALE: Many bugs occur at boundaries. EVALUATION CRITERIA: Compliant if tests include empty/zero/negative/MAX_VALUE or explicit edge names. DECISION RULES: 1) Look for boundary values like 0, -1, Integer.MAX_VALUE. 2) If all data are typical values, mark non-compliant. ANALYSIS: The test uses values 2784 and 1224 only; no zero, negative, empty, or max/min boundary checks are present. VERDICT: non-compliant.

PRINCIPLE: Tests should be self-contained and reuse helpers to remove duplication. RATIONALE: Reduces duplication and improves maintainability. EVALUATION CRITERIA: Compliant if helper methods or constants exist, or if tests are short and not repetitive. DECISION RULES: 1) Look for helper methods and constants. 2) If tests are very short and don't repeat code, mark compliant. ANALYSIS: The test is short (<10 lines) and self-contained; there is no evidence of duplicated blocks across multiple tests in the presented snippet. VERDICT: compliant

practices_evaluation.practice_title: Detailed Analysis of Size and Complexity
practices_evaluation.justification: PRINCIPLE: Keep tests small and low complexity. RATIONALE: Easier to understand and maintain. EVALUATION CRITERIA: Compliant if test methods are <20 lines with no loops/complex conditionals. DECISION RULES: 1) If method >30 lines or has loops/conditionals mark non-compliant. 2) If <15 lines and linear, mark compliant. ANALYSIS: The method is short, linear, and contains no loops or complex conditionals. VERDICT: compliant

PRINCIPLE: Assertions should be comprehensive to detect faults. RATIONALE: Superficial assertions can miss bugs. EVALUATION CRITERIA: Compliant if multiple properties of the result are asserted. DECISION RULES: 1) If only one assertion especially assertNotNull -> non-compliant. 2) If multiple properties verified, compliant. ANALYSIS: The test asserts peso(), v1(), v2(), and also checks numVertices() and notNull — multiple properties are checked. VERDICT: compliant

PRINCIPLE: Avoid @Ignore/@Disabled and commented-out tests. RATIONALE: Ignored tests hide problems. EVALUATION CRITERIA: Compliant if no @Ignore/@Disabled or commented-out @Test. DECISION RULES: 1) If @Ignore/@Disabled present mark non-compliant. 2) If all tests active, compliant. ANALYSIS: No @Ignore/@Disabled or commented-out tests are present in the shown method/class excerpt. VERDICT: compliant

PRINCIPLE: Link tests to requirements via comments/annotations. RATIONALE: Improves coverage tracking and impact analysis. EVALUATION CRITERIA: Compliant if @Story/@Requirement annotations or Javadoc with requirement IDs exist. DECISION RULES: 1) Look for @Story/@Requirement or Javadoc REQ- IDs. 2) If none, non-compliant. ANALYSIS: The class Javadoc includes 'Traceability: - REQ-GRAFO-001', satisfying traceability at class level. VERDICT: compliant

practices_evaluation.practice_title: Rigorous Use of Performance and Security Tests
practices_evaluation.justification: PRINCIPLE: Performance/security tests are separate from unit tests. RATIONALE: These are distinct concerns. EVALUATION CRITERIA: Compliant only if explicit performance/security tests exist; unit tests typically not applicable. DECISION RULES: 1) Unit tests are usually not-applicable. 2) Mark compliant only if explicit performance annotations or timing code present. ANALYSIS: This is a unit test for graph operations; no performance/security tests or annotations are present. VERDICT: not-applicable

PRINCIPLE: Test names should be descriptive of scenario and expected outcome. RATIONALE: Descriptive names aid maintainability and debugging. EVALUATION CRITERIA: Compliant if names follow methodName_scenario_expectedBehavior or BDD patterns. DECISION RULES: 1) If name follows pattern, compliant. 2) If generic name like test5, non-compliant. ANALYSIS: The method name 'test5' is generic and conveys no scenario or expected result. VERDICT: non-compliant.

practices_evaluation.practice_title: Small Footprint of Test Code Generation
practices_evaluation.justification: PRINCIPLE: Avoid verbose auto-generated tests; prefer concise intent-revealing tests. RATIONALE: Generated tests can be verbose and hard to maintain. EVALUATION CRITERIA: Non-compliant if signs of code generation exist (auto-generated comments, generic names like test0/test1, EvoSuite runner). DECISION RULES: 1) Look for auto-generated comments or repetitive names. 2) If found, mark non-compliant. ANALYSIS: The class uses EvoSuite runner (EvoRunner) and the method name is 'test5', indicating auto-generated origin despite an improved header. This signals auto-generation characteristics. VERDICT: non-compliant.

practices_evaluation.practice_title: Complete Prioritization of Test Case Design
practices_evaluation.justification: PRINCIPLE: Tests should show design intent (Given-When-Then or BDD naming) and be prioritized. RATIONALE: Thoughtful design leads to comprehensive coverage. EVALUATION CRITERIA: Compliant if Given-When-Then comments or BDD-style naming or multiple scenarios present. DECISION RULES: 1) If Given-When-Then or BDD naming found, compliant. 2) If only minimal happy path tests, non-compliant. ANALYSIS: Although the file header mentions Given-When-Then, the test method itself lacks such structure and only covers a single basic scenario; no evidence of prioritized or TDD/BDD-driven design in the method. VERDICT: non-compliant.

practices_evaluation.practice_title: Responsible Addition of Test Code Maintenance
practices_evaluation.justification: PRINCIPLE: Tests should focus on public API behavior and avoid testing implementation internals. RATIONALE: Reduces brittleness. EVALUATION CRITERIA: Compliant if tests call public methods and avoid reflection or private field checks. DECISION RULES: 1) If reflection used, non-compliant. 2) If only public methods used, compliant. ANALYSIS: The test calls public methods of Grafo and checks public behaviors; no reflection or private-state inspection is present. VERDICT: compliant

PRINCIPLE: Use clear, specific assertions, preferably with messages. RATIONALE: Specific assertions catch subtle faults and aid debugging. EVALUATION CRITERIA: Compliant if specific assertions (assertEquals/assertThat) are used; messages are a plus. DECISION RULES: 1) If >=50% assertions have messages, compliant. 2) If assertions are specific and clear even without messages, compliant. ANALYSIS: The test uses assertEquals and assertNotNull (specific assertions). No custom messages are used but assertions are specific and check multiple properties. VERDICT: compliant

PRINCIPLE: Comments should explain 'why' and not clutter obvious code. RATIONALE: Excessive or outdated comments are harmful. EVALUATION CRITERIA: Compliant when code is clean with minimal useful comments and no commented-out code. DECISION RULES: 1) If commented-out code found, non-compliant. 2) If code is clean and has useful class-level Javadoc, compliant. ANALYSIS: The class includes useful class-level Javadoc explaining intent and traceability; there is no commented-out code in the shown method. VERDICT: compliant

PRINCIPLE: Tests must be deterministic, avoid randomness/time/external deps. RATIONALE: Flaky tests erode confidence. EVALUATION CRITERIA: Compliant if no Random(), System.currentTimeMillis(), Thread.sleep(), or external dependencies without mocks. DECISION RULES: 1) If Random/System.currentTimeMillis/Thread.sleep found, non-compliant. 2) If none of these present and setup is local, compliant. ANALYSIS: The test uses deterministic calls to Grafo constructors and methods with no random/time/external deps. VERDICT: compliant

practices_evaluation.practice_title: Complete Avoidance of Test Side Effects
practices_evaluation.justification: PRINCIPLE: Tests must not leave persistent side effects or modify shared global state. RATIONALE: Side effects cause inter-test dependencies. EVALUATION CRITERIA: Compliant if only local variables used or @After cleanup present for external resources. DECISION RULES: 1) If @After cleanup present, compliant. 2) If persistent resources created without cleanup, non-compliant. ANALYSIS: The test creates a local Grafo instance and does not persist data or modify static state; no cleanup needed. VERDICT: compliant

practices_evaluation.practice_title: Suitable Utilization of Test Labels and Categories
practices_evaluation.justification: PRINCIPLE: Use labels/categories to organize tests for selective execution. RATIONALE: Enables targeted runs and CI efficiency. EVALUATION CRITERIA: Compliant if @Tag/@Category/@Category annotations present. DECISION RULES: 1) If @Category or @Tag found, compliant. 2) If none, non-compliant. ANALYSIS: The class is annotated with @Category(UnitTest.class) which provides categorization. VERDICT: compliant
